messages:
maya: heads-up — onboarding build for 'zephyr-v3-lite' (ptq) shows 4.7% structured-output failures on action invocations in the canary.

maya: failures look like ordering/positioning problems inside the 'actions' array (postprocessor expects first element to be 'call_tool'), but model sometimes emits the tool object later or duplicates a placeholder.

jonas: can you paste a raw example?

maya: sure — repro curl and response snippet: 
```
curl -X POST https://canary-api.redwood.ai/v1/invoke -d '{"prompt":"call weather", "mode":"action-only"}'

Response: {"id":"r1","actions":[{"note":"placeholder"},{"name":"get_weather","args":{"city":"SF"}}]}
```

maya: parser errors: "expected action[0].name == 'get_weather'" -> abort.

elaine: interesting. do we think quantization (ptq) is flipping token stream leading to suffix reordering? or is this sampling/artifact from batching?

todd: my hypothesis: intermittent chunking + streaming boundaries causing the model to emit a filler token object earlier, then the real action. If our ingestion assumes first-item semantics, it will break.

jonas: metric-wise, that's ~5% of canary calls — nontrivial. Any ETA on repro rate vs batch size?

maya: repro matrix: single-shot nonstreaming 0.5%, streaming w/ batch=8 ~4.7%, batch=32 ~6.2%. So scales with batching/stream size.

elaine: sounds like batching-induced reordering. Two short-term fixes: 1) make parser tolerant (match action objects by name/shape, not position) 2) adjust canary routing to reduce batching (disable continuous batching for this model) and retest.

todd: agree. Also propose a lightweight schema change: require an explicit 'index' field in each action object when we emit from high-risk models; that lets postproc reorder deterministically. For backward compatibility, parser should still accept missing index and fallback to name-match.

maya: implemented a quick patch in the postproc prototype to match by 'name' first then fallback to index. Local tests reduce aborts to 0.2% on streaming batch=8.

jonas: nice. What's the cost tradeoff if we disable batching? token-cost goes up; latency also. Need numbers for the SRE/infra doc.

maya: quick numbers: canary qps baseline 120 rps; disabling continuous batching for this model drops throughput to ~30 rps on same capacity, cost per 1k calls up ~+18%.

elaine: that's acceptable short-term for correctness during onboarding. Long-term we should aim to keep batching but make the runtime preserve per-request ordering or mark action boundaries at generation time.

todd: plan: A) roll postproc parser patch to canary (today) B) add index field to new model's eval harness (this week) C) run controlled canary with batching on/off and record structured-output compliance and cost per call (end of week).

maya: I'll push the parser patch to canary and kick off the canary job. tagging ci-bot: run structured-output-eval job against zephyr-v3-lite-canary (100k samples, stratified by prompt length and streaming flag).

ci-bot: queued structured-output-eval: job id 78642. estimated runtime 2h. results will post in #eng-ml when done. :robot_face:

jonas: also add a quick log sample capture (raw responses) for failed cases. We should store first 10k failures for manual inspection and model team feedback.

maya: done — collector on. will post a short summary once job completes.

elaine: good. follow-up: if index field approach works, we should add a small eval that simulates injected placeholder objects to stress the parser; canary should include that.

todd: agree. also add a note in onboarding checklist: "verify action ordering invariants under streaming + batching".

maya: thanks all — I'll update the onboarding doc and ping infra for capacity adjustments if we need to keep batching disabled longer.

jonas: thanks — looking forward to the CI results.
